source: data/amirnet-vocab.csv (Tier 1, A2) — K-005, alphabetical continuation from "rent" (the next_marker recorded in manifest-2026-09-16-4.json, verified live against the CSV and every existing batch-*.jsonl headword before writing — 316 Tier-1 single-word headwords were still missing at the start of this tick, none of the 15 written here existed under any batch file).
gate_method: gateSense (lib/core/contentSchema.ts) imported directly and run on every row via a temporary script (.scratch/checkgate.mjs, not pushed — deleted before commit) against the full draft set, using allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt. First-draft level drift (6 of 15 rows flagged on the first pass — background words not on the allow-list: email · grandfather · joyful · drummer (x2, example+item) · slippery · the number word "two") were fixed with allow-listed replacements and re-verified to 15/15. A negative control (7 extra rows, each broken on one distinct axis — Latin letters in translation_he, nikud in translation_he, headword missing from its own example, an item stem over the word limit with a level-drifting word, a stem with no blank marker, a stem that leaks the target word in its own body, two near_synonym distractors leaving fewer than 4 scorable) was run through the same checker immediately after the real 15/15 pass and correctly rejected on all 7 (0/7 passed) before any row was trusted.
distractor_allowed_words_note: Distractor words were checked by hand against allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt where practical (grep -x on the recurring "unrelated" pool: neighbor · garden · guitar · kitchen · mountain · jacket · chicken · coffee · bridge · forest · village · menu — all confirmed present), but this is a manual spot-check, not a mechanical gate: gateSense itself does not check distractor words against allowedWords at all, the same open gap recorded in every manifest since 12-13/09 (C-0545 onward).
he_one_to_many_note: "reply" (translation_he "מענה") deliberately avoids colliding with the existing headword "answer" (translation_he "תשובה", batch-2026-08-13.jsonl) by using a distinct, accurate Hebrew word rather than reusing "תשובה" — tagged in its own he_one_to_many_group field for traceability. "rhythm" was translated "מקצב" (not "קצב", already used by the existing headword "rate" sense 2, batch-2026-09-13-3.jsonl) for the same reason — checked live with grep against every existing translation_he in the bank before writing either row, so no untagged collision exists in this batch.
translation_confidence_note: 2 of 15 rows are translation_confidence:"medium" rather than "high": "retired" ("גמלאי" functions as a noun/adjective for a retired person and is not a 1:1 part-of-speech match for the English adjective — carries an he_interference_note distinguishing it from the unrelated homograph "פרוש"/"spread out") and "reunion" ("מפגש" is the natural, common word but is a general "meeting/gathering" — the narrower sense of "reunion after a long absence" is carried by the example sentences, not by the headword alone, and this is stated in its own he_interference_note). Neither is a guess: both are the correct, natural Hebrew word for the sense: the "medium" tag reflects the word choice being the best available fit rather than an exact one, per CONTENT.md STEP 5 ("never omit a word for uncertainty").
batch_size_note: 15 rows, one sense each, full apparatus (2 examples, 3 leveled items, 4 tagged distractors) per row.
